title: Pushes and pulls
examples: Teacher, when I pull a wagon, what force am I using?
If I kick a ball, is that a push or a pull?
Can you show me an example of a force that stops something?

explain.say: A force is a push or a pull.
When you push a toy car, you are using a force.
When you pull a wagon, you are using a pull force.
A force can make something start moving.
A force can also stop something that is moving.
When you open a door, you are usually pulling it towards you.

faq.q: Is opening a door always a pull?
faq.a: No, sometimes you might push the door open if it swings away from you. You must look at how the door moves to know the force.
asks: When is a door a push or a pull?
Does the door decide if it is a push or pull?

faq.a: Yes, if you push a rolling ball into a wall, the wall stops the ball using a force. This is called a stopping force.
asks: What stops a fast moving toy?
Can a push slow down movement?

faq.q: Are pushes and pulls always opposites?
faq.a: They are different types of forces, but they can work together. For example, you might pull a rope while pushing against it.
asks: Do pushes and pulls have to be opposite?
Can I use both a push and a pull at once?

faq.q: What is the difference between starting and stopping?
faq.a: Starting means making something move from being still. Stopping means making something that was moving become still again.
asks: How do I use force to stop something?

faq.q: Does the size of the push matter?
faq.a: Yes, a bigger push or pull is a stronger force. A small tap is a weak force.
asks: Is a big push better than a small push?

facts: A force can start an object that is at rest.
A force can stop an object that is moving.
A push is a force that moves something away from you.
A pull is a force that moves something towards you.

quiz.say: When you kick a football to make it move, are you using a push or a pull?
quiz.show: Kicking a ball: Push or Pull?
quiz.why: You kick the ball away from your foot, which is a push.

wrong.0: You are only doing one main action when you kick it.
wrong.2: Pulling suggests you are bringing the ball towards yourself.
wrong.3: A force must be either a push or a pull.

quiz.say: If a toy car is rolling, and you stop it by placing a block in front, what force is the block using?
quiz.why: The block pushes against the car, stopping its movement.

wrong.0: Rest is a state, not a force that stops movement.
wrong.1: A force is needed to change the car's motion.
wrong.3: Pulling would suggest the block is being dragged by the car.

quiz.say: When you open a drawer by grabbing the handle and pulling it out, what force are you using?
quiz.why: You are bringing the drawer towards you, which is a pull.

wrong.1: Pushing would mean you are forcing it away from you.
wrong.2: Start is what the force does, not the type of force.
wrong.3: The action is opening, not stopping.
